tagline: A bounded first-party product-analytics dashboard for one app
verdictSummary: First-party event tracking with funnels, retention, and basic cohorts is a genuine weekend-to-week build on an open time-series-friendly database. What doesn't survive: identity stitching across devices and sessions at scale, session replay, and the query performance Amplitude has engineered for billions of events.
coreLoopDIY: Collect custom events from one app's client SDK, store them durably, and compute funnels, retention curves, and basic cohort breakdowns from the raw event log.
whatYouLose: query performance at very high event volume
whyPeopleStillPay: A dashboard over your own events is buildable; making that dashboard stay fast and correct as event volume grows past what one database comfortably handles is where the engineering — and the subscription — actually goes.
prompt: Build a bounded, single-product event-analytics tool — not a general analytics platform. Use a lightweight browser SDK (a small JS snippet) that sends named custom events with arbitrary properties to your own ingestion endpoint. Use ClickHouse (genuinely well-suited to this — columnar storage makes funnel and retention queries fast even at moderate volume) or Postgres if you'd rather keep one database, with Next.js/TypeScript for the ingestion API and dashboard. Ingest events idempotently (dedupe by a client-generated event ID) and filter obvious bot traffic by user-agent pattern; do not fingerprint devices beyond a first-party, cookie-based anonymous ID. Build three dashboard views from the raw event table: a funnel builder (pick an ordered sequence of event names, see conversion between each step), a retention chart (percentage of a cohort that returns on day N), and a simple event-property breakdown (e.g. count of purchase events grouped by a plan property). Add a raw-event export and a data-deletion endpoint for a given anonymous ID, to keep this genuinely privacy-respecting rather than just smaller-scale surveillance. Do not build cross-device identity graphs, session replay, or a general BI/warehouse layer — those are out of scope; this tracks one product's events for one team, nothing broader. Requires hosting and a database (ClickHouse or Postgres); no external API key needed.

faq.q: Will it handle the event volume Amplitude does?
faq.a: For a single small-to-mid product, yes, especially with ClickHouse. It won't hold up at Amplitude's actual scale — hundreds of millions of events a day — without real infrastructure work beyond this prompt's scope.

faq.q: Does it track users across devices the way Amplitude's identity resolution does?
faq.a: No — this build uses a simple first-party anonymous ID per browser or device, with no cross-device stitching. That's a real capability gap, and also a meaningful privacy trade-off in your favor.

faq.q: Can I replay a user's session to see what they clicked?
faq.a: No, session replay isn't included — this tool only aggregates named events, not full interaction recordings.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting plus a database — a small self-hosted ClickHouse instance handles a meaningful amount of traffic cheaply, likely well under what a paid analytics seat costs per month.
